draft.title: Describing a distribution
card: Shape
A distribution is symmetric if both sides mirror each other. It is positively skewed if the tail stretches to the right, and negatively skewed if the tail stretches to the left.
Centre
The centre is the median (the middle value) or the mean (the average). In a skewed distribution, the mean is pulled towards the tail.
Spread
The spread is the IQR (Q3 − Q1) or the standard deviation. Median and IQR go together, as do mean and standard deviation.
Outliers
An outlier is a value far from the rest. Outliers pull the mean and standard deviation more than the median and IQR, so with skew or outliers, median and IQR are the better pair.
draft.remember: Describe shape, centre, spread and outliers, and use median and IQR when data is skewed.

a.q: Most scores in a histogram are bunched at the left, with a long tail to the right. What is the shape?
a.why: The tail names the skew, and this tail points right, so it is positively skewed. It is not negatively skewed, which has its tail on the left.
a.clue: Look at which way the tail points.

b.q: House prices in a suburb are positively skewed, with a few very expensive mansions. Which pair best describes centre and spread?
b.why: The mansions pull the mean and standard deviation upwards, so they misdescribe most houses. The median and IQR are less affected, and they are the matching pair.
b.clue: Which measures are pulled least by extreme values?
